name: GF
summary: The finite field with q elements, for a prime power q; F<a> := GF(q) names its generator a.
differs: Fields of more than a bounded size (in bits) are refused rather than built.

name: GF
summary: The finite field with p^n elements, for a prime p.
differs: Fields of more than a bounded size (in bits) are refused rather than built.

name: Characteristic
summary: The characteristic of a ring or field (0 for the integers and the rationals).

name: PrimitiveElement
summary: A generator of the multiplicative group of the finite field F.

name: Order
summary: The multiplicative order of a nonzero finite field element.

name: Degree
summary: The degree of the finite field F over its prime field.

name: PrimeField
summary: The prime field GF(p) of a finite field F of characteristic p.

examples.expected:
Finite field of size 2
Finite field of size 7

name: Generator
summary: The generator F.1 of a finite field over its prime field: a root of DefiningPolynomial(F), and 1 for GF(p) itself (not its primitive element).

name: Generator
summary: F.1, the generator of F over its subfield E (an error if E is not one).

examples.code: F<a> := GF(16); E<c> := GF(4); Generator(F, E);

name: DefiningPolynomial
summary: The defining polynomial of a finite field over its prime field: its Conway polynomial, and X - 1 for GF(p) itself.

name: DefiningPolynomial
summary: The minimal polynomial of F.1 over the subfield E of F.

examples.code: K<b> := GF(16); F<a> := GF(4); DefiningPolynomial(K, F);

differs: Relative to a proper subfield (not the prime field), only in fields of at most 2^20 elements; larger ones are refused.
Work is bounded (prime-field coefficient operations, counted before the first power): past the bound it is refused in words.

name: IsSubfield
summary: Whether F is a subfield of K: the same characteristic, and Degree(F) divides Degree(K).

name: Embed
summary: A procedure that checks F can be a subfield of K; Sagebrush's finite fields are already embedded in their overfields.
differs: Embed(F, K, x) with an explicit image is Magma's error (F is already a subfield of K).

name: Root
summary: A k-th root of x in its finite field (k > 0): the unique one when gcd(k, q - 1) = 1, else as Magma's where verified.
differs: When x has several k-th roots (gcd(k, q - 1) > 1), Magma's choice is reproduced only for k = 2 in GF(p) with p = 3 mod 4 and in GF(p^n), n > 1, of at most 3^12 elements; other such roots are refused.
Exponents of more than 1024 bits are refused (Magma takes them).
Work is bounded (prime-field coefficient operations, counted before the first power): past the bound it is refused in words.

name: Trace
summary: The trace of x over the prime field: x + x^p + ... + x^(p^(n-1)).
differs: Work is bounded (prime-field coefficient operations, counted before the first power): past the bound it is refused in words.

name: Trace
summary: The trace of x over the subfield F of its field.

examples.code: K<b> := GF(16); F<a> := GF(4); Trace(b, F);

differs: Relative to a proper subfield (not the prime field), only in fields of at most 2^20 elements; larger ones are refused.
Work is bounded (prime-field coefficient operations, counted before the first power): past the bound it is refused in words.

name: Norm
summary: The norm of x over the prime field: x^((q - 1)/(p - 1)).
differs: Work is bounded (prime-field coefficient operations, counted before the first power): past the bound it is refused in words.

name: Norm
summary: The norm of x over the subfield F of its field.

examples.code: K<b> := GF(16); F<a> := GF(4); Norm(b, F);

differs: Relative to a proper subfield (not the prime field), only in fields of at most 2^20 elements; larger ones are refused.
Work is bounded (prime-field coefficient operations, counted before the first power): past the bound it is refused in words.

name: MinimalPolynomial
summary: The minimal polynomial of x over the prime field: the product of X - c over its distinct conjugates c.
differs: Work is bounded (prime-field coefficient operations, counted before the first power): past the bound it is refused in words.

name: MinimalPolynomial
summary: The minimal polynomial of x over the subfield F of its field.

examples.code: K<b> := GF(16); F<a> := GF(4); MinimalPolynomial(b, F);

differs: Relative to a proper subfield (not the prime field), only in fields of at most 2^20 elements; larger ones are refused.
Work is bounded (prime-field coefficient operations, counted before the first power): past the bound it is refused in words.

name: CharacteristicPolynomial
summary: The characteristic polynomial of x over the prime field, of degree Degree(Parent(x)): a power of its minimal polynomial.
differs: Work is bounded (prime-field coefficient operations, counted before the first power): past the bound it is refused in words.

name: CharacteristicPolynomial
summary: The characteristic polynomial of x over the subfield F of its field.

examples.code: K<b> := GF(16); F<a> := GF(4); CharacteristicPolynomial(b^5, F);

differs: Relative to a proper subfield (not the prime field), only in fields of at most 2^20 elements; larger ones are refused.
Work is bounded (prime-field coefficient operations, counted before the first power): past the bound it is refused in words.

name: RootsInSplittingField
summary: The roots of f, over a finite field, in its splitting field, with multiplicities (by their logs, 0 first), and the field.
differs: Work is bounded (the factorization, then the roots, counted before each starts) and the splitting field has at most 2^20 elements: past these it is refused in words.
